verses.text: Then Job answered:
“I’ve heard plenty of talk like that. Every one of you is awful at comforting people!
Will this empty talk ever end? What’s got you so worked up that you have to answer?
I could talk just like you if we traded places. I could string words together against you and shake my head at you.
But I’d use my words to give you strength. What I said would ease your pain.
“Even when I speak, my grief doesn’t let up. And if I stay quiet, what relief do I get?
Now, God, you’ve worn me out. You’ve left everyone around me desolate.
You’ve shriveled me up, and that stands as a witness against me. My wasted body gets up and testifies right to my face.
In his anger he’s torn me apart and pursued me. He’s gnashed his teeth at me. My enemy fixes a sharp stare on me.
They gape at me with open mouths. They slap my cheek to shame me. They all gang up on me.
God hands me over to the godless and throws me into the grip of the wicked.
I was at ease, and he broke me apart. He grabbed me by the neck and smashed me to pieces. Then he set me up as his target.
His archers surround me. He splits open my kidneys without holding back. He spills my bile onto the ground.
He breaks through me again and again. He charges at me like a giant.
I’ve sewn sackcloth onto my skin and shoved my horn into the dust.
My face is red from crying, and deep darkness hangs over my eyelids,
even though my hands have done no violence and my prayer is pure.
“Earth, don’t cover up my blood. Let my cry never find a place to rest.
Look, even now my witness is in heaven. The one who vouches for me is on high.
My friends mock me. My eyes pour out tears to God,
that he would uphold a person’s rights before God, as one person would for a neighbor!
In just a few years, I’ll go down the road I can’t come back from.
